conviction_note: Mild positive lean (p_up 55) on a 5.5% absolute scale. The scale is rebuilt from eight confirmed prior prints (median |move| about 5.5%, 5 of 8 up), because the baseline history is 6-K text matches. The lean rests on company documents: FY consensus sits at the bottom of a guide that was set at a weaker peso than has prevailed, and the US carries a bearish segment consensus into a hurricane-free quarter. It is held near 50 because the last beat-and-raise (Q2) was sold -3.6%, energy costs rose after the guide, and most supporting items are proxies. impact_sum +1.2 is about twice the scaled +0.55; the gap is the reaction-function discount on the scaled number.
bar: Q3 2026 operating EBITDA US$953.9m and net sales US$4,506m: Cemex's own compiled consensus of 14 estimates, updated 2026-10-12 (https://www.cemex.com/en/investors/analyst-estimates). Segment EBITDA bars: Mexico 454.6 (+23% yoy), USA 252.0 (-6.4%), EMEA 254.3 (+2.9%), SCAC 67.5. FY2026 EBITDA 3,578 = +16.2% on 2025's 3,080, the low end of the company's 16-17% guide. A second source agrees: MarketScreener Q3 EBITDA 940.1, sales 4,403, FY 3,577 (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CEMEX-S-A-B-DE-C-V-6492888/finances/, 2026-10-22). MarketBeat EPS $0.25, revenue $4.45bn (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-26-cemex-sab-de-cv-stock/). Actinver expects EBITDA about +10% yoy (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/mercados/de-cemex-a-walmex-que-esperar-de-los-reportes-trimestrales-en-la-bolsa-mexicana/, 2026-10-18). The bar is sourced and the sources agree within 1.5%.
positioning_check: Short interest 15,650,424 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 52% from 10,287,321 on 09-15. That is about 1.1% of shares, 2.02 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/cx/short-interest). Not crowded, but building into the print. The option chain is unusable (ATM spread 167% of mid), so there is no skew and no implied move. Put/call OI 0.43. Tape: spot 10.06, -21% from the 12.72 close before the Q2 print, 25.8% below the 52-week high, 20-day run-up +3.6%, 5-day -1.85%. Sell-side: Citi upgraded to Buy on 10-15 (target cut 13.70 to 12.00); RBC trimmed to 13.25 on 10-09; mean target about 38% above spot.

findings.finding: Cemex's FY2026 guide (EBITDA +16-17%, raised 2026-07-23) assumes MXN 18.25-18.50 per USD for 2H26. Banxico's FIX was 17.1277 on 2026-09-14, per Cemex's own dividend 6-K, about 6.5% stronger. Consensus FY EBITDA of 3,578 (+16.2%) still sits at the very bottom of the guide range (3,573-3,604 on 3,080). Mexico is about 50% of consensus FY EBITDA (1,785 of 3,578). So delivering the plan at prevailing FX points to a reiterated-top or raised range, against a bar priced for the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has moved this stock the most. The Q3 2024 guide cut fell -8.7% (close 2024-10-25 5.98 to 10-28 5.46). The Q3 2025 beat with record margins rose +9.9% (9.36 to 10.29, 2025-10-28). But the Q2 2026 raise to 16-17%, together with an EBITDA beat (1,018 vs about 937 consensus), fell -3.6% (12.72 to 12.26, 2026-07-23). Prices are from Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CX?range=2y&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: Fourteen analysts updated by 10-12 still model FY at +16.2%, the guide floor, so the consensus has not credited the FX gap. If the market had priced a guide-top outcome, FY consensus would sit at 3,600+ and the stock would not be 21% below its post-Q2 level with targets cut. Caveat built into the size: analysts likely already model spot FX, so the low-end consensus may reflect expected underlying slippage (energy, US), not overlooked FX.
findings.independence: The guide and its FX assumption are from the Q2 6-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001076378/000119312526313194/d46310dex1.htm, 2026-07-23). The consensus table is from https://www.cemex.com/en/investors/analyst-estimates (2026-10-12). Peso level confirmed independently: eldolar.info shows 17.78 on 2026-09-28 (https://www.eldolar.info/es-MX/mexico/dia/20260928).

findings.finding: Mexico's construction output rose 7.3% yoy in July and 7.5% in August 2026, with civil engineering +17.6% in August (INEGI industrial activity release of 2026-10-12, via Trading Economics). The Q2 call guided that Mexico's temporary share gains would normalise in 2H and that the margin would dip slightly. Consensus Mexico Q3 EBITDA is 454.6 (+23% yoy, mostly FX) on sales of 1,283 (+14.8%), below Q2's actual 491.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mexico drove the Q1 2026 print (+6.3%, 11.77 to 12.51 on 2026-04-23) and was the strongest segment in Q2 (+27% LTL EBITDA), yet Q2 still traded -3.6% on the US miss. Net of the rest: the US (-6% consensus) and EMEA (+3%) would have to disappoint by more than any Mexico upside for the total to miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry series, not a company number. If it were priced, the Mexico consensus would sit at or above Q2's 491 rather than 7% below it. Sized small because it is a proxy, and management itself pre-warned of share normalisation.
findings.independence: CANACEM said Mexican cement sales grew 2% in 1H26 (https://globalcement.com/news/21201-mexican-cement-industry-grows-by-2-in-the-first-half-of-2026), a slower industry rate than the construction series. Actinver and B×+ expect Mexico efficiency gains (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/mercados/de-cemex-a-walmex-que-esperar-de-los-reportes-trimestrales-en-la-bolsa-mexicana/).

findings.finding: The first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 (Isaias) formed only on 2026-10-07, the latest first hurricane on record, so Q3 had no hurricane disruption. On the Q2 call Cemex said 2H US margins should improve if the hurricane season does not disrupt. It also said the Q2 one-offs (temporary aggregate purchases for an Arizona project, a 7% rise in cement imports) would not repeat, and that a mid-single-digit SoCal/Arizona price increase starts in July. Consensus US Q3 EBITDA is 252.0, -6.4% yoy, against a record-margin Q3 2025 comp of 269.3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US EBITDA -11% in Q2 2026 coincided with the -3.6% reaction despite a consolidated beat, so the market trades the US line. Net of the rest: a US beat of $10-15m is about 1-1.5% of consolidated EBITDA.
findings.why_not_priced: A US consensus still below prior year after the Omega acquisition was consolidated suggests analysts carried Q2's weakness forward without crediting the stated non-recurring items or the quiet weather. Weather is an inference, so the finding is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call transcript summary on US one-offs and price increases (https://www.webull.com/news/15279684413957120, 2026-07-23). USGS: US cement shipments +9.8% yoy in June, +5.1% in 1H26 (https://www.cemnet.com/News/story/182292/us-and-puerto-rican-cement-market-expands-10-in-june.html).

findings.finding: Brent settled at $104.61 on 2026-09-12 after touching $107-109 that week, with US diesel at historic highs. It had been about $83-88 in late July, when Cemex guided cement energy cost only low-single-digit up and 2H energy costs about +4% (about -$20m). About 60% of 2026 energy spend was hedged (Q1 call) and about 80% of 2027 diesel. The risk lands on the 2H/2027 cost commentary and on the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned explicitly on energy. Cemex fell -8.7% on the Q3 2024 guide cut, which is the downside template if the guide is trimmed.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Seeking Alpha attributes the 30% drawdown from the May high partly to energy costs (https://seekingalpha.com/mp/1061-the-insiders-forum/articles/6346585-cemex-s-a-b-de-c-v-a-deep-dive, 2026-10-04). Kiln fuels (petcoke, coal) track oil only loosely, and hedges defer the hit. Sized small: it is macro-to-company transmission the company has not quantified since July.
findings.independence: TASS: Brent fell below $83 on 2026-07-28 for the first time since 07-17 (https://tass.com/economy/2166539/amp). Hedge levels are from the Q1 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-3-31-cemex-sab-de-cv-stock/) and the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15279684413957120).

findings.finding: JPMorgan's Elodie Rall expects Q3 2026 volumes at European building-materials companies to fall on average versus Q2, on heat-related summer site closures, partly offset by price increases. Cemex EMEA consensus is 254.3 (+2.9% yoy) against a record-margin Q3 2025, and Q2 EMEA was already flat-margined on heat-hit volumes once the $42m one-off is excluded.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EMEA was not the swing line on recent prints. It carried the Q3 2025 beat (+9.9%). Net of the rest: EMEA is about 27% of Q3 consensus EBITDA.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a sell-side view on peers, so it is likely reflected in Cemex's modest EMEA consensus. It is a proxy and sized small. Heidelberg's own Q3 update (2026-11-04) falls after the window.
findings.independence: The Q2 call says the European heat wave restricted work hours and softer demand hit several markets (https://www.webull.com/news/15279684413957120).

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is -21% from the pre-Q2 close (12.72 to 10.05) and 26% off its 52-week high, while FY EBITDA consensus stayed at the guide (3,578). Short interest jumped 52% to 15.65m shares at the 09-30 settlement (still only about 1.1% of shares, 2.0 days to cover), and Citi moved to Buy on 2026-10-15. The price discounts a worse outcome than the published estimates do.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2024 print came off a depressed base (about $6) and moved +13.4% (5.98 to 6.78, 2025-02-06). The Q2 2026 print came off a high base (12.72) and fell -3.6% on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The gap between a price that fell 21% and estimates that did not move is the market's own statement, so this is partly the price itself, and it is sized small. A short rebuild of 5m shares on about 7.7m ADV is a small squeeze fuel at best.
findings.independence: Citi upgrade and target cut on 10-15 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/robeco-boosts-cemex-stake-citi-cuts-target-for-cemex-stock-to-usd-12-00/70382737, 2026-10-21). MarketBeat 200-day moving average 11.65 against spot about 10.06 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-cemex-cx-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/).

findings.finding: An aggregator reports that director Zambrano Lozano bought 400,800 Cemex shares for '6.93 million USD', reported on 2026-09-25. The implied $17.29 per unit matches the CPO price in pesos, not USD, so this is most likely a purchase of about MXN 6.9m (about USD 0.4m) of CPOs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No insider-buy history found for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Already public for a month. The amount is tiny relative to a $14.9bn market cap and the currency is garbled; it signals insider willingness near the lows and nothing more.
findings.independence: None. I could not find the BMV insider filing. Cemex's 2026-09-18 BMV notice says no board member traded around that day's unusual volume (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1076378/000119312526395792/d185749d6k.htm).

findings.finding: On 2026-07-20 the European Commission sent Cemex a Statement of Objections over alleged 2021-22 price coordination in its admixtures business in France and Germany. Cemex says it cannot assess the outcome or materiality, so a provision or an update could appear in the Q3 release or 6-K notes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on this. Cemex called the sales under investigation insignificant.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since July. Any provision would sit below operating EBITDA, and a fine decision is far beyond the window. Sized as a small one-off.
findings.independence: Concurrences on the Commission's SO to construction-chemicals makers (https://www.concurrences.com/en/bulletin/news-issues/july-2026/the-eu-commission-sends-a-statement-of-objections-to-several-construction).

outside_window.finding: The Colombia divestment to Holcim (US$485m plus about US$70m of other sales) is expected to close at year-end. Closing and use of proceeds would be later catalysts, though the release may update timing.
Heidelberg Materials' Q3 2026 trading update on 2026-11-04 is the next European read-across.
A competitor's Mexico plant may restart in Q4, per the Q2 call. That is a 2027 pricing and share risk, and may surface in the outlook.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Baseline reaction history (median 1.33%, 1 of 8 up) as the reaction scale
rejected_candidates.detail: The rows are dividend and other 6-Ks (for example 2026-09-04 and 09-14 are dividend notices, per the SEC filings). Real prints rebuilt from Yahoo bars: -3.6, +6.3, -1.2, +9.9, +3.5, +4.6, +13.4, -8.7; median |move| about 5.5%.

rejected_candidates.candidate: MXN 17.78 on 2026-09-28 implies the peso weakened in late September, which would shrink finding 1
rejected_candidates.detail: Same FX fact as finding 1. Even at 17.78 the peso is still about 3-4% stronger than the 18.25-18.50 guide assumption; folded into finding 1's range.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Data-centre demand: 35% of US mega data-centre projects in Cemex's footprint; ready-mix to data centres doubled in 1H26
rejected_candidates.detail: A structural theme stated by management on the Q2 call, so it is public. Folded into the US view (finding 3) rather than counted separately.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or implied move to cut against. The modest positive lean runs against the 21% slide since Q2 and the rising short interest. I treat that slide as the price discounting energy and US risk, and the published estimates as not following it, which leaves room for relief if the guide holds. The Q2 beat-and-raise being sold keeps p_up near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; Q2 beat-and-raise was sold -3.6%): Mexico construction finding 0.6 to 0.5, US hurricane finding 0.4 to 0.3, p_up 56 to 55
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the energy finding is partly priced per the drawdown attribution, so -0.8 to -0.6
Lesson 5 (a drawdown/positioning gap is an inference, not a document): positioning finding +0.5 to +0.3; CX is not a microcap and the drawdown has stated causes, so it stays filed
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar was already sourced to the company's own 14-estimate consensus plus MarketScreener, which agree; no cap needed
Lesson 'reaction history built from the wrong events': the base rate was already rebuilt from confirmed prints before drafting; no change

Lessons 2, 4, 7, 8, 9 left standing: the antitrust item is already a small one-off; no financing; no skew and no crowded short; coverage is broad (14 estimates); segment findings already stated net of the rest
